evidence.note: Row D45 is the joint over both routes to the state this lane names: a decision that DOES list the item but no longer authorizes it. D4 reaches it by direct JSON write - the real applier performs the withdrawal, then a raw writeFileSync on scope-shrinkage-decision.json flips decision to rejected and userConfirmed to false while leaving withdrawnChecklistItemRefs untouched. D5 reaches the identical state through the CLI, a second scope_shrinkage_decision_set with decision=rejected whose union logic carries the refs forward. Both are still refused by BOTH gates. Row C8 measures the premise that makes this non-vacuous: in both fixtures the record STILL lists the item while withdrawnChecklistItemIdsFrom resolves to the empty set, so what is measured is the authorization test and not a vanished ref - exactly what a bare withdrawnChecklistItemRefs.includes(id) shortcut would still honour. Ablation: replacing the helper with new Set(decision.withdrawnChecklistItemRefs) in dist turns D45 BYPASSED while B1/B2/B3 and all ten controls stay green, and the three D1..D3 rows stay REFUSED, so this row is independently load-bearing. Selector is the stable row id and stays REFUSED after the fix.

commands.label: B-45a5 standing regression guard (was CHK-001's RED artifact): three clauses, all mandatory. (1) Both REVIEW-path gates must keep EXCLUDING an item-level withdrawal authorized by a confirmed decision. (2) Both must keep biting on everything that is NOT withdrawn, including an item that merely shares an authored verificationIntent id alias with a withdrawn one. (3) Both must keep REFUSING every UNBACKED withdrawal: a status flipped by hand with no decisionRef, a dangling decisionRef, a decisionRef naming a real decision that does not list the item, or a decision overwritten to decision=rejected / userConfirmed=false. Clause 3 is the safety-critical one: without it the withdrawal mechanism is forgeable by hand-editing a JSON status field. Exits 1 if any clause regresses, 2 if a control/premise breaks. CHK-003 removed the pre-fix optional flag, so this is now mandatory
